title: Plurality Is Stablest for Small Positive Correlations: A Gaussian Simplex Theorem
summary: For each fixed number of cells, proves a dimension-independent qualitative interval of small positive correlations on which the balanced regular-simplex partition maximizes Gaussian noise stability, with equality rigidity.
verification: Analytic all-cell proof, including the attributed first-moment covariance argument, with published geometric inputs. abstract:
Zhang proved regular-simplex optimality for the sum of squared Gaussian
cell first moments for every $k\ge2$, including the $k\ge4$ endpoint.
Building on his theorem, we prove that, for every fixed $k\ge2$, the central
regular-simplex partition maximizes Gaussian noise stability among all
equal-measure measurable $k$-cell partitions in every dimension $d\ge k-1$,
for all sufficiently small positive correlations. The interval is independent
of $d$, and equality determines the simplex partition up to orthogonal maps,
labels and cylindrical extension. Our contribution is the passage from
first-moment optimality to positive-correlation optimality using compactness
for measurable label changes normalized by their exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck
score loss. Weighted Gaussian tightness yields a limiting facet flux whose
sharp quadratic cost forces rotationality; moment alignment removes that
mode. The threshold is qualitative and may depend on the number of cells.
